‘Woojinga the Chambers’, a Korean beef restaurant located near Yeoksam Station

It has several private rooms, making it a great place to dine these days, and both the exterior and interior of the store are painted in dark black tones, giving it a luxurious and sophisticated feel.

This place sells meat per gram, but on this day, I ate sirloin and striploin first and then ordered salchisal.

When you order meat, a dedicated server will grill it so you can enjoy your meal comfortably.
Both the sirloin and strip loin were amazing as they were thick from the looks of it. In particular, this place was grilled over charcoal, so you could feel the flavor even more.
What about the salchisal that I ordered afterwards... the taste you imagine melting in your mouth👍

I think the biggest advantage of this place is that it is corkage-free, but even though it is corkage-free, it is impressive that a glass of Riedel is provided.
Also, many Korean beef restaurants in a similar price range do not use charcoal, but using charcoal is a big advantage.

Although the price is a bit high at 38,000 won per 100g of sirloin, I was satisfied with the many advantages such as a private environment and corkage-free policy.

reviews.author: Chanwook Lee
reviews.text:
Katsu8 is said to have been given the name because the time at which tonkatsu is most deliciously fried is 8 minutes. Although it has only just opened, it is already a famous tonkatsu restaurant in the Gangnam area and recently opened a branch in Yongsan.

When I looked at the menu, I had a hard time choosing between fish katsu and assorted katsu. However, it was an attractive option because there was an assorted cutlet that came with sirloin, tenderloin cutlet, cheese cutlet, and fried shrimp all at once.

The assorted katsu consists of katsu, rice, miso soup, cabbage salad, and tartar sauce salad. Sauces and ground sesame seeds are neatly placed on each table so you can use them when needed.

Cheese Katsu is filled with fresh mozzarella cheese inside pork. The savory cheese adds softness and moistness without compromising the natural taste and juiciness of the pork and goes well with the meat.

The shrimp used in fried shrimp are tiger shrimp, a member of the king shrimp family, and they are so large that they make your mouth water. It's not fried shrimp, which is mostly fried, but the shrimp meat is so plump that you can put it in your mouth and chew it.

Both the tenderloin cutlet and sirloin cutlet were cooked to a good standard. I think it's one of the best tonkatsu I've ever eaten because it's fried for the optimal time of 8 minutes, and the batter has a nice golden brown color.

reviews.author: Because he’s a genius
reviews.text:
It's rare to find a place to gather in Gangnam, but this house has a room so it's great for business meetings or quiet drinks.
The service is also smooth, so there are no major issues.
However, we are holding off on recommending it as a destination for a ‘taste tour’.
After eating, the first thing that comes to mind is, “The space and service are nice... but what was the most memorable thing?”

Definitely a compliment to the beer.
Kirin Draft Beer (9,000) has excellent pouring, and the foam texture, temperature, and carbonation are among the top tier Kirin beer I've tried in Korea.
Terra Draft Beer (6,000) was also neat with good line and temperature management.
With empty words, I couldn't help but think, "You could change your job to a beer bar."

Aged sashimi (75,000/3 people) is ambiguous at first impression.
The quantity was (too) thin compared to the price, and the inclusion of salmon was a bit of a surprise.
Ironically, the salmon and cuttlefish were in good condition.

The tuna akami was okay, the flounder was above average thanks to the fish itself, and the sweet shrimp was small but still sweet.
On the other hand, the portion of abalone is small and the crab sauce is fishy, ​​and the herring/mackerel series is too passive at one point, so the aftertaste is short.

The twist is the Ankimo Canapé (19,000).
The portion is generous and the maturation tone is clean, making it feel like spreading well-ripened blue cheese on a cracker.
A sip of beer—the endless loop of a canapé is both painful and enjoyable.
However, it is not the type that boldly pushes aging, so you may like it or not (or feel it tasteless).

Isobe Maki is made by rolling mackerel sashimi in seaweed and pulling it well without fishy fish.
However, the volume and presence are again disappointing.

Overall, the impression that “the taste is not bad, but the volume and impact is lacking compared to the price” follows you until the end.
Corkage is not cheap, so it is difficult for the advantages of ‘clean room or neat service’ to be a cheating point.
In conclusion, it's a good candidate when you urgently need a gathering space, but if you want to get excited about sushi, I'd choose another place first.

reviews.text:
I ordered regular curry udon and butter mushroom curry.

The basic base here is beef. In other words, I ordered beef curry udon.

The first taste was that of a commonly known curry, but before I knew it, the all-too-familiar taste continued to linger. It took me so long to recognize this taste because it was so familiar to me.

In fact, since I wrote it down, people who read my review would naturally know that it was the beef flavor of beef fat, but in fact, I largely overlooked this because even if beef was added to the menu name, the beef flavor was rarely applied to the entire menu.

Also, when ordering curry udon, they add a yolk in the middle, and I really liked that when I mixed it slightly and ate it with the yolk, the savory sweetness became more noticeable. I immediately understood why they eat the yolk together.

In other places, curry and udon tasted like separate dishes, but this was a restaurant with the quality that finally allowed me to recognize the perfect curry udon meal as food. Plus, there are unlimited rice refills, so all you have to do is finish the udon and eat the rice. At this time, quite thick beef toppings are sinking to the bottom, and the pleasure of eating them with a spoon along with the rice is guaranteed. So I recommend udon.

If you want to experience the true, deep taste of beef curry, I definitely recommend this restaurant.

Then I tried the coconut mushroom beef curry, but I liked the regular curry better, with the deep beef flavor.

I added less coconut than expected, so the flavor and greasiness were not that noticeable, so the balance was good, but I think there was a reverse synergy in that the meat flavor of the beef was reduced compared to the beef curry. For that menu, I think it would have been better to give it a distinctly greasy taste rather than narrowing down one's likes and dislikes.

Of course, this is only when comparing the two curries, and the butter curry was delicious enough.

As a side menu, the tonkatsu was served in mini size, which was reasonably priced at 4,000 won. It was okay to eat as a side, but it was far behind in tonkatsu specialty restaurants... It was a regular tonkatsu. I don't remember exactly, but I think there were other sides, so if you don't really want tonkatsu, try something else.

I ate puffer fish soup, which is famous at Gangnam Station. I visited Akasaka Japanese Restaurant because I wanted some hot soup in the chilly weather. Without hesitation, I ordered the signature dish, Bokguk Hansang, and it was an excellent choice. It was served in a clear Jiri style, and the soup was so refreshing and deep, with the fragrant scent of water parsley spreading throughout. 🐡 It's the best as a hangover, but it also felt like I was taking good care of myself. It was really good value for money for 16,000 won.
The pufferfish flesh was so firm and chewy that I could immediately feel in my mouth that they used fresh ingredients. The side dishes that came with it were all neat and tasty, so I emptied the entire bowl of rice in no time. The cod roe, blowfish, karaage, and special ponzu were all very good. The store was clean and the service was friendly, so it was a pleasant meal. If you are looking for a proper pufferfish restaurant and hearty Japanese food, I highly recommend Akasaka Japanese Food Bokguk Hansang.

My first visit to the Yeoksam branch of Ginjako, which has quite a few chain stores.
This is a place where I usually order delivery...
Even though it was almost 1:30 after lunch time,
There were two teams waiting.
When I wondered why, the space was rather narrow.
It's not that it's inconvenient to eat, but the cafeteria itself is rather small, so it's a fast food restaurant that fills up with about 15 people.

The location is in a corner, near the outdoor unit, so it's a pain to wait in the summer, so if there's a long wait, it might be better to look at the next opportunity.

Orders are placed at the kiosk just to the right of the entrance.
The price is pretty good.
The most expensive lunch menu is 19,000 won. The name of the menu is Jumbo Demi Pork Cutlet and it comes with 5 pieces.
Not recommended unless you are a big eater. However, what is unique is that it is provided additionally in the form of poached eggs.
Even the basic portion is quite filling for the average person.
In fact, there are many people who leave a comment.
Kimchi and jangguk are served on their own along with unlimited refills and water.
Kimchi goes well with pork cutlet.
Since the sauce is based on demi-glace sauce, it can't be helped that it gets sticky if you eat a lot, so I ended up eating kimchi.
Since it comes with mustard sauce, it cuts down on the greasiness quite well.

It's good value for money and has a unique taste, so I recommend it if the wait isn't long.

The atmosphere isn't bad and there are some seats, but it's narrow, so you end up bumping into people a bit when walking back and forth.

reviews.author: chan hyoung kim
reviews.text:
# Basic information
-Visit date: 2026/01/20 Lunch
-Characteristics: Due to the nature of the area near Yeoksam Station, it is mainly open for lunch

# space atmosphere
-It is a typical counter seat configuration in Japan and is equipped with shichimi (spicy), garlic chips, pickled garlic (ragyo), and pickled radish (fukujinzuke). Looking at the dishcloths used to wipe the tables and the tsukemono set, it appears that a strong Japanese atmosphere was intended.
-While waiting for my food while looking at the furniture and fixtures, I was able to feel as if I was at a Japanese curry restaurant. I was looking forward to it.
-However, the use of low-quality wooden tables and the unharmonious combination of wooden colors leave something to be desired. Even though it has only been two days since opening, the texture of the table that touches your hand is not good. This may have to be understood as an implementation of a Japanese low-cost chain curry restaurant.

# Order Menu
Karaage curry + added rice

#Food Taste
-My first impression was that something was very wrong. From the first bite, the salinity is felt to be quite high, and soon a strong sweetness appears. This is followed by the spicy scent of turmeric and the scent of herbs such as oregano. I think excessive salt and sugar levels are beyond the realm of taste. After eating about half of it, it is so sweet, salty, and thick that it becomes difficult to lift a spoon. Overall, the ‘assertiveness’ of the taste is so strong that it is burdensome.
-Bob didn't go well either. It's a curry restaurant in name, but I don't know why the rice is so weak. Rather than the rice being tough, the grains were crushed. I didn't feel like the grains were being chewed.
-Karaage is freshly fried and very hot and crispy, but the meat is thin. It tastes ordinary.
Karaage, which is crispy fried but has a soft, cushiony texture on the inside and juicy meat, can only be eaten in places that are quite good in Japan, and perhaps because the evaluation standards have been lowered due to disappointment with the taste of curry, there were no major complaints about the karaage itself.
-However, the cream sauce on top of the karaage (a crazy sweet sauce that looks like cooking cream or mayonnaise mixed with yeondu) made the already spicy curry even more burdensome.

# Services and Operations
-The number of employees is relatively large compared to the size of the store. Greet guests loudly when they come in or leave. It was a good attempt to provide a lively response, but it felt like there was no balance between the bustle of the ramen shop and the identity of the place.
-Despite the fact that there were approximately 20 seats and about 6 employees, the employees were unable to determine what the customers had ordered, possibly due to the kiosk ordering system. It was quite an interesting system to see customers being asked about the menu each time they served food. It appears that they have not yet learned the efficiency or meticulousness of Japanese-style operation.

# Price and satisfaction
-The quality of the curry was not special and satisfaction was also low. As it is still in the early stages of opening, there is room for improvement by accepting feedback, but compared to other curry restaurants that put effort into combining all the spices themselves and extracting the flavoring oil, it is child's play.
-Personally, I wonder how many opportunities will be given to a store that only pretends to be Japanese on the outside and uses solid curry and sweetener during lunch hours for office workers in Yeoksam.
-Personally, I commute to the Gangnam area, so I live with understanding and consideration even when it comes to substandard food. The Gangnam area is full of restaurants with poor quality for the price, but if you look at them one by one, there is no place to eat. Here too, rather than imposing high standards, I wrote down what I felt based on general standards.
- I think it would be a good idea to lower the level of stimulation to the point where you wonder, ‘Is this okay?’ and then re-establish the taste from the basics. Rather than hoping for a fluke, I think we can survive by bringing out the flavor that is faithful to the basics.
